title: Genesis Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who was born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaac
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:3 states that Abraham called the name of his son born to him by Sarah, Isaac.

questions.question: At what age was Isaac circumcised according to God's command?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight days old
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:4 says Abraham circumcised Isaac when he was eight days old as God commanded.

questions.question: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
questions.correctAnswer: 100 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:5 clearly states Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac was born.

questions.question: What did Sarah say God had made her do?
questions.correctAnswer: Laugh
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:6 says Sarah said God made her laugh, so that everyone who hears will laugh with her.

questions.question: True or False: Sarah was surprised that she was able to nurse a child in her old age.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:7 shows Sarah expressing surprise that she had borne Abraham a son and could give him suck in her old age.

questions.question: What event did Abraham celebrate with a great feast?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaac being weaned
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:8 states Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

questions.question: Who did Sarah see mocking her son Isaac?
options: The son of Hagar the Egyptian
questions.correctAnswer: The son of Hagar the Egyptian
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:9 says Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian mocking Isaac.

questions.question: What did Sarah ask Abraham to do to the bondwoman and her son?
questions.correctAnswer: Cast them out
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:10 states Sarah told Abraham to cast out the bondwoman and her son.

questions.question: True or False: Abraham was pleased and not grieved at casting out the bondwoman and her son.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:11 indicates it was very grievous to Abraham because of his son.

questions.question: According to God, in whose seed shall Abraham's seed be called?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaac
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:12 says God told Abraham that in Isaac shall his seed be called.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to make a nation of the son of the bondwoman because he is Abraham's seed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:13 states God would also make a nation of the son of the bondwoman because he is Abraham's seed.

questions.question: What did Abraham give Hagar when he sent her away?
options: Bread and a bottle of water
questions.correctAnswer: Bread and a bottle of water
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:14 says Abraham took bread and a bottle of water and gave them to Hagar when he sent her away.

questions.question: What did Hagar do when the water was spent and she was in the wilderness?
options: She cast the child under a shrub and wept
questions.correctAnswer: She cast the child under a shrub and wept
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:15-16 describes Hagar casting the child under a shrub and sitting afar off, weeping.

questions.question: In Genesis 21, which event comes first?
options: Abraham makes a covenant with Abimelech
Hagar and her son are sent away
questions.correctAnswer: Sarah conceives Isaac
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:2 states Sarah conceived and bore Isaac before later events such as the weaning (verse 8) and covenant with Abimelech (verse 22).

questions.question: True or False: Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac was born.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:5 confirms Abraham was one hundred years old at Isaac's birth.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did God promise Abraham regarding the son of the bondwoman according to Genesis 21:13?
options: He would be ignored and forgotten
He would become a great king in Egypt
God would make a nation of him because he is Abraham's seed
He would live a life of hardship without descendants
questions.correctAnswer: God would make a nation of him because he is Abraham's seed
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:13 states that God promised to make a nation of the son of the bondwoman because he is Abraham's seed, highlighting God's faithfulness to all of Abraham's descendants.

questions.question: What items did Abraham give to Hagar when he sent her away, and what does this teach about obedience and care?
options: Bread and a bottle of water, showing provision despite difficult obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Bread and a bottle of water, showing provision despite difficult obedience
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:14 records that Abraham gave Hagar bread and a bottle of water, indicating that even when obeying hard commands, provision and care are maintained. This teaches us about faithful obedience with compassion.

questions.question: According to Genesis 21:15-16, how did Hagar react when the water was spent and her child was in danger?
options: She cast the child under a shrub and wept, sitting a bowshot away
She sent the child away alone
She went back to Abraham for help
questions.correctAnswer: She cast the child under a shrub and wept, sitting a bowshot away
questions.explanation: These verses show Hagar’s despair and faith struggle as she distances herself physically but weeps loudly, reflecting the human experience of sorrow and trust in God during trials.

questions.question: What does Genesis 21:17-18 reveal about God's response to Hagar and her child?
options: God told them to return to Abraham immediately
God heard the child’s voice, reassured Hagar through an angel, and promised to make the child a great nation
God punished them for leaving Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: God heard the child’s voice, reassured Hagar through an angel, and promised to make the child a great nation
questions.explanation: These verses show God's attentive care and reassurance through the angel, demonstrating His faithfulness and protection even in desperate circumstances.

questions.question: How did God help Hagar find water, and what does this teach about divine provision according to Genesis 21:19?
options: God guided her with a star
God opened her eyes to see a well of water
God sent a man with water
God instructed her to dig a new well
questions.correctAnswer: God opened her eyes to see a well of water
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:19 illustrates that God directly provided for Hagar by revealing a well, teaching that God provides in unexpected ways when we trust Him.

questions.question: According to Genesis 21:20-21, what was the future life of Hagar's son, and what does this tell us about God's blessing?
options: He became a king in Egypt
He died young in the wilderness
He grew, became an archer, and took a wife from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: He grew, became an archer, and took a wife from Egypt
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize God's ongoing blessing and presence with Hagar’s son, leading to growth and establishment of his own family, showing God’s faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: What did Abimelech and Phichol say to Abraham in Genesis 21:22, and what virtue does this demonstrate?
options: They acknowledged that God was with Abraham in all he did
They demanded Abraham leave their land immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They acknowledged that God was with Abraham in all he did
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:22 shows recognition of God's favor on Abraham, teaching the virtue of integrity and respect for God's work in others.

questions.question: What was Abimelech's request to Abraham in Genesis 21:23, and how does this relate to biblical principles of integrity and kindness?
options: To swear not to deal falsely with him or his descendants, showing a desire for honest and kind relations
questions.correctAnswer: To swear not to deal falsely with him or his descendants, showing a desire for honest and kind relations
questions.explanation: This verse highlights the importance of making covenants based on honesty and kindness, reflecting Godly principles of integrity and mutual respect.

questions.question: How did Abraham respond to Abimelech's request in Genesis 21:24, and what does this teach about honoring commitments?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Abraham agreed to swear as requested (Genesis 21:24), demonstrating obedience and the biblical virtue of honoring one’s commitments.

questions.question: Why did Abraham reprove Abimelech according to Genesis 21:25, and what does this teach about standing up for justice?
options: Because Abimelech's servants violently took away a well of water
Because Abimelech refused to make peace
questions.correctAnswer: Because Abimelech's servants violently took away a well of water
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:25 shows Abraham standing firm against wrongdoing to protect his rights, teaching the importance of seeking justice respectfully.

questions.question: What was Abimelech's reaction when Abraham reproved him in Genesis 21:26?
options: He claimed ignorance of the incident until that day
questions.correctAnswer: He claimed ignorance of the incident until that day
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:26 illustrates Abimelech's honest response showing he was unaware, exemplifying humility and openness to correction.

questions.question: What did Abraham give Abimelech to confirm their covenant, and what does this signify about biblical agreements according to Genesis 21:27-28?
options: Sheep and oxen, and seven ewe lambs as witnesses
questions.correctAnswer: Sheep and oxen, and seven ewe lambs as witnesses
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:27-28 shows Abraham giving livestock to seal the covenant, with the seven ewe lambs serving as a tangible witness, teaching the seriousness of making and honoring agreements.

questions.question: What meaning did Abraham give to the place where the covenant was made in Genesis 21:31?
options: It was named Beersheba, meaning 'Well of the Oath'
questions.correctAnswer: It was named Beersheba, meaning 'Well of the Oath'
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:31 explains that the place was called Beersheba because that is where they swore the oath, signifying the importance of covenant commitments.

questions.question: How does Genesis 21:33 teach us about Abraham's attitude toward God after making the covenant?
options: He forgot about God and focused on wealth
He planted a grove and called on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God, showing reverence and worship
questions.correctAnswer: He planted a grove and called on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God, showing reverence and worship
questions.explanation: This verse shows Abraham honoring God with worship and remembrance, teaching us to respond to God's faithfulness with reverence.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 21:14-19, what does God's provision for Hagar and her son teach us about trusting God in difficult circumstances?
options: God provides for and protects even those in wilderness and despair
Human effort is the only solution
questions.correctAnswer: God provides for and protects even those in wilderness and despair
questions.explanation: These verses together show God's active care in desperate situations, encouraging trust in His provision and faithfulness.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 21.

questions.question: What grievance did Abraham express to Abimelech in Genesis 21:25?
options: The theft of livestock by Abimelech’s servants
The violent taking of a well of water by Abimelech’s servants
The refusal of Abimelech to make a covenant with him
The mocking of Isaac by Abimelech’s servants
questions.correctAnswer: The violent taking of a well of water by Abimelech’s servants
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:25 explains that Abraham reproved Abimelech because his servants had violently taken away a well of water.

questions.question: How did Abimelech respond when Abraham confronted him about the well in Genesis 21:26?
options: He admitted his guilt and apologized
He claimed ignorance, saying he did not know who did it
questions.correctAnswer: He claimed ignorance, saying he did not know who did it
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:26 records Abimelech saying he did not know who had done the thing, nor had he been told about it until that day.

questions.question: What did Abraham give to Abimelech as part of their covenant in Genesis 21:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Sheep and oxen
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:27 states that Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech as part of their covenant agreement.

questions.question: Why did Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart in Genesis 21:28?
options: As a witness to the covenant regarding the well
To give as gifts to Abimelech
To offer as a peace offering
questions.correctAnswer: As a witness to the covenant regarding the well
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:28-30 explain that Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart so that they might be a witness that he had dug the well.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Beersheba' as explained in Genesis 21:31?
options: It means 'Well of seven' because of the seven lambs
It signifies the place where Abraham and Abimelech swore an oath
It is the city where Isaac was weaned
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the place where Abraham and Abimelech swore an oath
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:31 states that the place was called Beersheba because there both Abraham and Abimelech swore an oath.

questions.question: What action did Abraham take at Beersheba after making the covenant, according to Genesis 21:33?
options: He built an altar to sacrifice Isaac
He planted a grove and called on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God
He constructed a well for water
questions.correctAnswer: He planted a grove and called on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:33 tells us Abraham planted a grove at Beersheba and called on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.

questions.question: How long did Abraham sojourn in the land of the Philistines as per Genesis 21:34?
questions.correctAnswer: Many days
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:34 simply states that Abraham sojourned many days in the land of the Philistines.

questions.question: In the narrative of Genesis 21, the covenant between Abraham and Abimelech exemplifies which ancient Near Eastern cultural practice?
options: The establishment of a treaty sealed with livestock as witnesses
The use of written contracts on stone tablets
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of a treaty sealed with livestock as witnesses
questions.explanation: The practice of sealing covenants with animals as witnesses, as seen with the ewe lambs in Genesis 21:28-30, reflects common ancient Near Eastern treaty customs.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Genesis 21:6 where Sarah says, 'God hath made me to laugh,' and what does it signify?
options: Irony, highlighting the unexpected joy of childbirth in old age
Metaphor, comparing God to a jester
Chiasm, emphasizing the reversal of fortune
questions.correctAnswer: Irony, highlighting the unexpected joy of childbirth in old age
questions.explanation: Sarah’s statement in Genesis 21:6 is ironic because laughter is unexpected in her old age but signifies joyous fulfillment of God’s promise.

questions.question: What is the original Hebrew meaning of the name 'Isaac' as given in Genesis 21:3 and 21:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Laughter
questions.explanation: In Genesis 21:3 and 21:6, Isaac’s name is connected to laughter, reflecting the Hebrew root צָחַק (tsachaq), meaning 'to laugh.'

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's promise and fulfillment seen in the birth of Isaac in Genesis 21?
options: Romans 4:18-21, where Abraham’s faith is commended for believing God's promise
Acts 2:1-4, the coming of the Holy Spirit
John 3:16, God’s love for the world
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 4:18-21, where Abraham’s faith is commended for believing God's promise
questions.explanation: Romans 4:18-21 reflects on Abraham’s faith in God’s promise despite his and Sarah’s old age, paralleling Genesis 21's fulfillment of that promise.

questions.question: How does the story of Hagar and her son in Genesis 21:14-21 foreshadow later biblical themes of God's care for the marginalized?
options: It illustrates God’s providence for the outcast and covenant descendants alike
It prefigures the exile of Israel to Babylon
It symbolizes the division between Jews and Gentiles
It serves as a warning against disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God’s providence for the outcast and covenant descendants alike
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:17-19 shows God hearing Hagar’s distress and providing water, foreshadowing biblical themes of divine care for the marginalized and the establishment of a nation through her son.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 21:12, God instructed Abraham to listen to Sarah because Isaac would be the one through whom Abraham’s descendants would be named.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:12 clearly records God telling Abraham to heed Sarah's voice because through Isaac his seed shall be called.

questions.question: True or False: Abraham refused to make a covenant with Abimelech because of the dispute over the well in Genesis 21.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Contrary to refusing, Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech as recorded in Genesis 21:27-32, resolving their dispute over the well peacefully.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar covenant-making ceremony involving seven animals as seen in Genesis 21:28-30?
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:3-6 describes a covenant ceremony involving the setting apart of animals, similar to the seven ewe lambs in Genesis 21:28-30, illustrating a common covenant practice.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God visiting Sarah and fulfilling His promise to her as recorded in Genesis 21:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God's Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:1 shows God's faithfulness because He visited Sarah and did exactly as He had spoken, fulfilling His promise without failure or delay.

questions.question: According to Genesis 21:4, what covenantal practice did Abraham perform on Isaac, and what doctrine does this signify?
options: Circumcision; signifying the covenant of grace
questions.correctAnswer: Circumcision; signifying the covenant of grace
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:4 records Abraham circumcising Isaac at eight days old as commanded by God, signifying the covenant of grace promised to Abraham's seed, a foundational doctrine of God's covenantal relationship with His people.

questions.question: How does Sarah's reaction to Isaac's birth in Genesis 21:6 reflect a theological truth about God's intervention in human weakness?
questions.correctAnswer: God transforms despair into joy
questions.explanation: Sarah says God made her laugh so all that hear will laugh with her (Genesis 21:6), showing God's power to bring joy and hope where there was previously barrenness and despair, reflecting His grace and sovereign intervention.

questions.question: What theological principle about inheritance and election is taught by God's instruction to Abraham regarding Isaac and Ishmael in Genesis 21:12-13?
options: Only the oldest son inherits blessings
Election is based on human effort
God's election follows His sovereign will, not human lineage
Both sons share equally in the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God's election follows His sovereign will, not human lineage
questions.explanation: In Genesis 21:12-13, God instructs Abraham to heed Sarah because the covenant seed is through Isaac, not Ishmael, teaching that God's election and promises follow His sovereign choice rather than natural descent or human effort.

questions.question: In Genesis 21:17-19, which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by His hearing the voice of Ishmael and providing water in the wilderness?
questions.correctAnswer: God's Compassion
questions.explanation: God hears the voice of the lad Ishmael and provides a well of water (Genesis 21:17-19), demonstrating His compassion and care even for those outside the primary covenant line.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's providence is illustrated by Abraham's covenant with Abimelech in Genesis 21:27-31?
options: God ordains peace and justice among nations
God's providence is limited to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains peace and justice among nations
questions.explanation: The covenant between Abraham and Abimelech (Genesis 21:27-31) reflects God's providence extending to ordering peace and justice among Gentile nations, affirming His sovereign rule over all peoples.

questions.question: How does the chapter's narrative concerning Hagar and Ishmael (Genesis 21:14-21) foreshadow the broader biblical theme of God's care for the marginalized?
options: God punishes all outside the covenant
God protects and blesses the marginalized
questions.correctAnswer: God protects and blesses the marginalized
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:14-21 shows God hearing the cries of Hagar and Ishmael, providing water and promising to make Ishmael a great nation, foreshadowing God's concern for those marginalized and outside the immediate covenant line.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story of Abraham sending away Hagar and Ishmael is evidence of divine cruelty. What does Genesis 21:10-13 and 17-19 actually teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God is indifferent to human suffering
God balances justice with mercy by protecting Ishmael while upholding the covenant through Isaac
questions.correctAnswer: God balances justice with mercy by protecting Ishmael while upholding the covenant through Isaac
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:10-13 and 17-19 show God instructing Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away to protect the covenant through Isaac, yet God also hears Ishmael's cries and provides for him, demonstrating both justice in covenant faithfulness and mercy toward Ishmael.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God's covenant faithfulness and human responsibility is drawn from Genesis 21:3 and Genesis 21:24-25?
options: God's covenant is unconditional and human action is irrelevant
Human effort alone secures God's promises
God's covenant faithfulness invites human response and covenant renewal
God's promises are symbolic and not binding
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant faithfulness invites human response and covenant renewal
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:3 shows Abraham naming Isaac as God commanded, reflecting covenant faithfulness, and Genesis 21:24-25 records Abraham swearing a covenant with Abimelech, demonstrating human responsibility to uphold covenant relationships alongside God's faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Abraham's planting of a grove and calling on the name of the LORD in Genesis 21:33 relate to the doctrine of worship and God's eternal nature?
options: It signifies rejection of God's eternal nature
It reveals worship as acknowledgment of God's everlasting nature
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals worship as acknowledgment of God's everlasting nature
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:33 shows Abraham planting a grove and calling on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God, affirming worship as recognizing God's eternal, unchanging nature and our continual dependence on Him.

questions.question: What does Genesis 21:5 teach about God's power in relation to human limitations, particularly concerning Abraham's age and Isaac's birth?
options: God's power is limited by human age
God cannot fulfill promises to the elderly
God transcends human limitations and fulfills His promises
God only works through young people
questions.correctAnswer: God transcends human limitations and fulfills His promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:5 emphasizes Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born, illustrating that God's power transcends natural human limitations such as advanced age to accomplish His divine promises.

questions.question: What theological significance does the weaning of Isaac and the associated feast in Genesis 21:8 convey about covenantal joy and communal celebration?
options: Covenantal joy is private and secretive
Communal celebration is unrelated to God's promises
The feast marks covenantal joy and public acknowledgment of God's blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The feast marks covenantal joy and public acknowledgment of God's blessings
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:8 describes Abraham making a great feast when Isaac was weaned, signifying covenantal joy and communal celebration as a public acknowledgment of God's blessing and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Genesis 21:20-21 reflect the doctrine of God's providential care beyond the immediate covenant community?
options: God abandons those outside the covenant
God is providentially involved in the growth and welfare of Ishmael's descendants
questions.correctAnswer: God is providentially involved in the growth and welfare of Ishmael's descendants
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:20-21 shows God was with Ishmael as he grew and settled in the wilderness, indicating God's providential care extends beyond the covenant community to all His creation.

questions.question: What does the naming of the place Beersheba in Genesis 21:31-32 symbolize in the broader narrative of covenant and divine faithfulness?
options: It marks a place of conflict and division
It signifies a solemn covenant and divine oath between Abraham and Abimelech
It is unrelated to covenant theology
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies a solemn covenant and divine oath between Abraham and Abimelech
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:31-32 shows the naming of Beersheba as the place where both Abraham and Abimelech swore a covenant, symbolizing a solemn divine oath and God's faithfulness to uphold covenant promises in relationships among peoples.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God's promise and human obedience is drawn from Genesis 21:2 and Genesis 21:4?
options: God's promises occur regardless of human obedience
Human obedience is irrelevant to God's covenant
God's promises are fulfilled in the context of obedient covenantal action
questions.correctAnswer: God's promises are fulfilled in the context of obedient covenantal action
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:2 records Sarah conceiving at God's appointed time, and Genesis 21:4 records Abraham circumcising Isaac as God commanded, together teaching that God's promises are realized through faithful human obedience within covenant frameworks.
